cut_items.item: States what the prune command removes: stopped containers, unused networks, unused images, build cache, unused volumes
Says Docker asks for confirmation and that -f skips it
Says running containers are not removed by the prune command
Advises using docker system df to compare disk usage before and after
Lists what the prune command deletes: stopped containers, unused networks, unused images, build cache, unused volumes
Mentions -f flag skips confirmation for the basic prune command
Explicitly states running containers are not removed by the prune command
Suggests checking docker system df before and after to measure space freed
Claims --volumes with system prune removes only anonymous volumes and suggests docker volume prune -a for named volumes (for system prune this is a different/less precise claim)

added_items.item: Defines 'unused' and explains that stopped containers are removed first, so their images become unused too
Gives a step-by-step safe procedure: check with docker system df, run prune, confirm with y, and Docker prints the space reclaimed
Full-reset sequence also includes docker rmi -f for all images and docker volume rm for all volumes
Warns that images will be downloaded again on the next pull or build
Troubleshooting: the 'docker rm requires at least 1 argument' error means nothing of that type exists and can be ignored
Troubleshooting: an image in use by a container cannot be removed until that container is removed first
Specifies the version in which docker volume prune changed to remove only anonymous volumes (Docker 23+), and that -a removes named volumes with that command
Gives the Docker Desktop settings path (Settings, Resources, Disk image size)
Defines 'unused' (not used by a running container) and explains stopped containers are removed first so their images become unused
Step-by-step safe workflow: run docker system df first, then prune, then confirm with y and see space reclaimed
Explicit note that the command is permanent and to check what you need first
Full reset sequence also removes images (docker rmi -f $(docker images -aq)) and volumes explicitly (docker volume rm $(docker volume ls -q)), including stop of all containers
Warning that the next docker pull/build will re-download images
Troubleshooting: 'docker rm requires at least 1 argument' error just means nothing of that type exists
Troubleshooting: image cannot be removed if a container uses it; remove the container first
Docker Desktop: specific Settings > Resources path and 'Disk image size' to shrink disk
Correctly states docker volume prune without -a removes only anonymous volumes on Docker 23+, and -a is needed for named volumes (with version number)
